title: Blest Is the Man, for Ever Blest
description: Blest Is the Man, for Ever Blest in Tonic Solfa to WINCHESTER NEW, doh is C: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 4 verses and a piano.
about: Isaac Watts wrote these words for The Psalms of David Imitated in the Language of the New Testament (1719): Psalm 32, part 3, headed “Repentance and free pardon; or, Justification and sanctification”.
Watts' psalms were printed without tunes and sung to any tune of their metre, Long Metre (8.8.8.8). This page sets the words to WINCHESTER NEW; any other Long Metre tune fits them as well.
underlay: Blest is the man, for ev-er blest, Whose guilt is par-don'd by his God, Whose sins with sor-row are con-fess'd, And cov-er'd with his Sav-iour's blood.

lines: Blest is the man, for ever blest,
Whose guilt is pardon'd by his God,
Whose sins with sorrow are confess'd,
And cover'd with his Saviour's blood.
Blest is the man to whom the Lord
He pleads no merit of reward,
And not on works, but grace relies.
From guile his heart and lips are free,
His humble joy, his holy fear,
And join to prove his faith sincere.
That hides and cancels all his sins!
While a bright evidence of grace
Thro' his whole life appears and shines.

source: Isaac Watts, The Psalms of David Imitated (1719)
licence: Public domain: Isaac Watts died in 1748.
credits: Words by Isaac Watts (1674–1748), public domain; set to WINCHESTER NEW by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
